title: Adaptive GPU Budget Mediator: Spill-to-Host + KV Slimming for Stable Continuous Batching
creator: Ava Liu
description: Problem: As mixed-tenant workloads with continuous batching increase, we regularly hit transient GPU memory pressure points where we must choose between dropping requests, degrading latency, or performing heavy-weight evictions. Current hard-cut eviction policies and blunt KV eviction cause QoS variability and worse overall token throughput. Goal: Implement a mediator that dynamically negotiates per-model/per-tenant memory budgets across weights, KV cache, and activations, and applies a prioritized mitigation stack: light-weight KV slimming, predictive compression, and if necessary, spill-to-host with predictable latency tails. The mediator should integrate with runtime schedulers, autoscaler hints, and Console telemetry for visibility.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mediator runs as a low-latency in-process decision layer on GPU hosts and returns a memory-action within 2ms for >99% of requests. 2) Under mixed load stress tests, overall P95 token latency increases by <=10% while token throughput drop <=5% relative to baseline without mediator. 3) KV slimming modes (trim-prefetch, drop-nonessential-keys, reduced-key-precision) reduce KV footprint by at least 25% on high-pressure scenarios with measured quality impact <2% (user-defined eval). 4) Spill-to-host triggers only when predicted headroom <5% for next 10s window and falls back to local actions when host I/O is degraded. 5) All actions emitted to Console traces and cost dashboard with per-cause counters and time series.
design_notes:
- Mediator architecture: lightweight policy engine + predictor. Policy engine consumes telemetry (current allocs, running batches, KV hit rates, model quantization profile) and outputs actions: 'slim-kv', 'compress-kv', 'defer-batch', 'spill-activations-to-host', 'preempt-burst'.
- Predictive model: short horizon (10s) time-series predictor built from token arrival rates and historical headroom; start with linear-AR features then iterate to small LSTM if needed.
- KV slimming modes: (a) metadata-only trim, (b) reduce embedding precision (float32->int8) for low-impact keys, (c) evict age-low-access keys first, (d) probabilistic sampling for large cold keys. Slimming operates at shard-level to avoid hot rebalances.
- Spill-to-host design: use pinned staging buffers on NVMe with async DMA paths; predictable per-token tail budget configured per-class-of-service. Provide fallback to compressed local cache if NVMe busy.
- Contracts: mediator must respect reserved weight memory and never evict model weights. It only moves/adjusts KV and activations.
- Telemetry: expose predicted_headroom, action_taken, pre/post footprints, and model-quality delta tags on traces.
- Safety: actions have soft timeouts; mediator reclaims aggressive modes after stable window (configurable).
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
- Alternative: global static quotas per-tenant. Rejected because it can't adapt to bursty continuous batching and leads to underutilization.
- Alternative: always spill-to-host first. Rejected due to I/O tail risks and cost.
- Tradeoff: We allow limited lossy KV slimming because compressed or reduced-precision KV can impact generation quality; to mitigate we couple with per-prompt eval metrics and a kill-switch injection if quality regressions exceed thresholds.
- Resource tradeoff: predictor accuracy vs CPU overhead. Initially prefer cheap predictors to minimize scheduler interference.

open_questions:
1) What quality evals should gate lossy KV slimming for each model class? Suggest default eval set per model family and allow tenant override.
2) Operator knobs for spill-cost accounting: how to surface cross-tenant NVMe contention in billing?
3) When to escalate to autoscaler (request more GPU RAM) vs keep applying local mitigations? Define heuristic thresholds.
4) Should mediator be centralized per-host or a cross-host coordinator for colocated tenant fairness? Start per-host, evaluate coordinator later.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for policy engine, predictor simulation, and each KV slimming mode.
- Synthetic stress tests: concurrent RTT-heavy requests + long-context requests to exercise KV growth. Run 24h replay tests.
- Chaos tests: inject NVMe stalls and verify spill-to-host fallbacks trigger compression and do not crash runtime.
- Quality regression tests: run prompt sets for representative models and track generation score delta pre/post slimming.
- Perf criteria: collect 50k tokens across mixes to measure P50/P95 latency and throughput delta.
rollout_plan: 1) Stage in internal staging cluster (done). 2) Canary on two Dedicated clusters (1% traffic each) for 72h, monitor headroom predictions, action rates, P95. 3) Increase to 10% traffic for tenants opting in; run nightly regression. 4) Full release behind runtime-1.22 toggle after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no quality regressions > threshold. 5) Provide opt-out tenant flag and per-tenant policy overrides.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Spill-to-host introduces tail latency. Mitigate: batch spill operations, limit concurrent spills, fall back to local compression.
- Risk: Lossy KV slimming causes subtle quality degradations. Mitigate: conservative defaults + per-model gating + automatic rollback on eval alerts.
- Risk: Mediator CPU overhead affects serving. Mitigate: keep decision path sub-2ms and offload heavier predictors asynchronously.
- Risk: NVMe contention across tenants. Mitigate: per-tenant spill slots and backpressure signals to Console for billing/ops.

owner_notes: Keep the mediator surface minimal and reversible. Prioritize conservative actions first (slim/compress) before spill. Instrument everything; we should be able to answer 'why did you evict that key?' for any action taken.
